record.title: REACT reports target-free event-stream collision-time estimates at 4.6 ms latency
record.summary: Keime, Cuperlier and Cottereau report REACT, a fully spiking state-space model that updates from raw event-camera streams without temporal accumulation. On the EvTTC validation split, their v1 preprint reports 9.59±0.74% relative time-to-collision error and 4.6 ms end-to-end latency without a target-box prior. The authors report 4 cm of travel during that latency at the dataset mean approach speed of 9.22 m/s; at 100 km/h the same latency corresponds to 12.8 cm. Their INT8 energy figures are analytical estimates, not hardware measurements. The numerical results are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that REACT processes raw events sequentially with continuous-time spiking state-space dynamics, without event accumulation or target-box input.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On EvTTC, the authors report 9.59±0.74% relative TTC error and 4.6 ms end-to-end latency; 4 cm travel uses dataset mean speed 9.22 m/s, while 12.8 cm uses 100 km/h.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report 25.7% relative TTC error on one FCWD sequence without fine-tuning; energy figures are analytical estimates based on a 45 nm proxy and await hardware validation.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the EvTTC evaluation or reported latency was performed; exact test sequences, preprocessing, runtime hardware and measurement details are not independently checked.
Energy results use a 45 nm analytical proxy; no physical neuromorphic hardware or robotic-platform measurement is reported in the inspected source.
The test set is limited and zero-shot transfer covers one FCWD sequence; generalization to varied speeds, scenes, sensors and closed-loop robot behavior is not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported target-free, event-by-event collision-time performance generalizes, it could change perception latency and sensing architecture choices for reactive robots. Consequence is meaningful within event-based robotics; evaluation scope is narrow and deployment evidence is absent.
limitations: All reported performance values are from the authors’ arXiv v1 preprint and have not been independently reproduced.
The 9.59% EvTTC comparison changes input regime relative to target-box baselines; do not present it as a fully matched same-input win.
The 4 cm and 12.8 cm distance figures use different vehicle-speed assumptions and should not be compared as conflicting measurements.
The INT8 energy estimate is a proxy and should not be described as measured device energy.
The authors promise code on publication; the inspected paper does not provide a public implementation.
brief.summary: Keime, Cuperlier and Cottereau report REACT, a fully spiking state-space model that updates from raw event-camera streams without temporal accumulation. On the EvTTC validation split, their v1 preprint reports 9.59±0.74% relative time-to-collision error and 4.6 ms end-to-end latency without a target-box prior. The authors report 4 cm of travel during that latency at the dataset mean approach speed of 9.22 m/s; at 100 km/h the same latency corresponds to 12.8 cm. Their INT8 energy figures are analytical estimates, not hardware measurements. The numerical results are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced.

technical.claimed_result: The preprint reports 9.59±0.74% relative TTC error at 4.6 ms end-to-end latency on EvTTC without a target bounding box. It reports 4 cm vehicle travel at 9.22 m/s dataset mean speed; the 12.8 cm value uses the same latency at 100 km/h. INT8 quantization reports 10.26±0.81% error and an estimated 2.8 mJ per 32,768 events.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected arXiv v1 source documents the architecture, experiment tables and author-reported results. No independent reproduction, physical neuromorphic measurement, or real-robot deployment was inspected.
technical.mechanism: Each raw event updates a spiking state-space model; physical inter-event time drives complex C-SiLIF continuous-time dynamics, avoiding fixed temporal accumulation.
technical.regime: EvTTC validation split; FCWD zero-shot transfer; DVS128-Gesture. Reported metrics aggregate three gesture seeds/five EvTTC seeds as stated by authors. Latency is end-to-end in the paper’s evaluation; hardware platform detail and external replication were not verified.
technical.reproducibility: No public code was linked in the inspected v1 HTML; the authors say code will be made public upon publication. Cheapest next check: inspect arXiv revisions and the authors’ repository for code, then reproduce the EvTTC table with matched sensor, sequence and preprocessing details.
technical.strongest_baseline: EvTTC comparison in Table II includes Garl-TTC at 9.44% and 113 ms with event+frame input and target box; REACT uses events only and no target prior. The comparison changes inputs and task setup, so it is informative but not a fully matched causal comparison.

brief.title: REACT reports target-free event-stream collision-time estimates at 4.6 ms latency
brief.why_it_matters: A model that predicts collision timing continuously from raw events without first detecting or tracking a target could shorten the perception-to-action path in fast reactive robotics. The reported accuracy is close to target-box-based learned methods under a different input regime, but this remains a single preprint evaluation on limited driving data; real-robot utility and hardware energy are not established.
